highlights.title: Meta is making Muse more powerful and will let you video chat with it, too
highlights.summary: Meta is quickly iterating on its new Muse AI agent, announcing a bunch of updates today that make the bot more capable and able to chat with you in more ways. Muse agents are getting their own email addresses that they can use for accomplishing tasks.
body: Muse started as a chatbot but will soon be an AI avatar you can talk with over video.

Meta is also going to give you another way to chat with its popular AI agent: video calls. Since its recent launch, the primary way to talk with Muse was through a chat interface, but you’ll soon be able to have live video conversations with your Muse avatar. Meta will let you tweak the way your Muse avatar sounds — you can already customize the way it looks — and a new Muse Realtime Avatar model will inform how it moves.

Muse launched earlier this month, and it’s seemingly proving to be a hit, topping the App Store charts and reportedly being downloaded more than ChatGPT on mobile in its first 12 days. Meta appears to be capitalizing on the popularity by quickly introducing the new videocalling features, but that’s not all that’s new for the agent. Meta says it plans to launch Muse on its smart glasses in the coming months, which will let you talk to Muse about what you’re looking at while wearing your glasses.

highlights.title: Kaptein scores winner as Chelsea earn narrow victory over Austria Wien
highlights.summary: Wieke Kaptein scored a stunning goal but Chelsea were given a stern test by Austria Wien as they began their Women's Champions League campaign with a hard-fought 1-0 win at Plough Lane.
body: Chelsea went ahead in spectacular style early on. Sandy Baltimore's run was ended by a well-timed sliding tackle and the ball spun loose. Collecting it 25 yards from goal was Kaptein, and after taking a touch she hammered it in off the bar.
Keira Walsh was forced off injured after 20 minutes, a potential blow for Chelsea ahead of Sunday's WSL game at home to Arsenal.

The home side were living dangerously when goalkeeper Livia Peng fumbled a shot from a short corner routine, palming the ball back out into danger from where Virginia Kirchberger hoisted it over the bar.
There was almost a sublime equaliser when Louise Schoffel danced her way through Chelsea's defence and hit a low shot that flashed inches wide of the post.

highlights.title: Warner Bros. Pushes Back DC's Dynamic Duo Film, Gremlins 3 Gets One Year Delay
highlights.summary: Warner Bros. has pushed back DC's Dynamic Duo and delayed Gremlins 3 by a whole year. Warner Bros. is preparing its 2028 slate, which has resulted in a couple of movies shifting their release dates around.
body: The new Gremlins will be directed by Chris Columbus, who wrote the original Gremlins and helmed classic films like Home Alone. Not much is known about the next film in the franchise, but it's a project Columbus has pursued for over a decade. It will likely be a while longer before we get any more meaningful footage, given it's now two years away from hitting theaters.

DC's experimental Robins movie Dynamic Duo, which will follow Dick Grayson and Jason Todd's early adventures, is also moving its date. The film was originally slated for June 2028, but will now open on September 22, 2028. The film is expected to be a hybrid between traditional CG animation, stop motion, and puppetry, giving it a unique visual style. The Batman director Matt Reeves and current DC Studios boss James Gunn will both produce the film.

It seems like this may be DC's attempt at trying to make something similar to the Spider-Verse films, leveraging younger characters with a unique visual style. Whether there's as much interest in an animated Robins project as there was for a character like Spider-Man remains to be seen.

Littler has taken a stance against volatile crowds before, refusing to travel to European Tour events in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there.

highlights.summary: YouTube is launching a new feature that allows creators to test different cuts of their own videos, leading fans to worry that it could be used for weaponized negativity. Earlier today, YouTube unveiled a bunch of new features coming for creators in 2027.
body: Some have feared that this may encourage creators to test videos that skew positively or negatively before deciding which one gets the most traffic and using that as the permanent choice. One example provided by someone on X is someone making a YouTube video where they review the upcoming remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time with a positive and a negative review.

This has also led some to wonder how this might be reflected to viewers. Will some audiences watch completely different videos and be left wondering what others are referring to in the comments or on social media? All in all, the feature poses some flaws, but hopefully YouTube can prevent it from being abused.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

highlights.title: Elizabeth Holmes to Be Moved From Prison to Halfway House in 2027
highlights.summary: The disgraced Theranos founder will be placed in an Austin-area facility in August 2027 as she serves out her reduced sentence for defrauding investors.
body: Elizabeth Holmes, the imprisoned founder of Theranos who duped investors with a claim to have revolutionized blood testing and was sentenced to more than 11 years for fraud, will reportedly be moved from a Texas prison into a halfway house in 2027.

On Wednesday, ABC News reported that Holmes is scheduled to be placed in the Austin Transitional Center in Del Valle, Texas, on Aug. 23, 2027. The network cited an update from the Department of Justice’s Victim Notification System.

Known for her strikingly deep, husky baritone voice and uniform black wardrobe, Holmes was a Silicon Valley icon as the proprietary technology Theranos said it invented was primed to disrupt modern medicine. But a 2015 Wall Street Journal investigation found that Theranos’ proprietary technology was a ruse, and only a dozen of the hundreds of tests it offered were actually being performed. In fact, the company relied on third-party devices and traditional blood testing to perform what it said was its industry-shattering tech.
Following the company’s decline, Holmes went from Silicon Valley wunderkind to epitomize a “fake it ’til you make it” mentality that permeated the tech industry.

highlights.title: A US-China AI Hotline Won't Be Ready For a While
highlights.summary: As the US and China race to become the dominant power in the AI industry, the countries also appear to be figuring out ways to communicate on national security issues.
body: As US president Donald Trump and Chinese president Xi Jinping prepare to meet in Washington for a state dinner at the White House on Thursday, AI has become a top priority. Tech executives from OpenAI and Nvidia have confirmed their attendance at the dinner, as a number of key agenda items are on the table.

Chief among them is a US proposal to establish an AI notification system with China, akin to the Cold War hotline with Moscow, which would allow each country to alert the other about national security issues related to AI. Treasury secretary Scott Bessent first announced the notification system on Sunday with Chinese vice premier He Lifeng.

But for all the high-level progress, Trump administration officials tell Inner Loop they expect it to still take a number of weeks to finalize an agreement, even if they are optimistic that the hotline could be in place before the year’s end.

There are several parts that need to be formalized in more detail, including establishing benchmarks on what kind of incident rises to the level of a national security issue, which remains unclear, as well as explicit sign-on from China, which has been noncommittal.
points: As the US and China race to become the dominant power in the AI industry, the countries also appear to be figuring out ways to communicate on national security issues.

highlights.title: Artist Behind Pokémon 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR Card Gives Tearful Response to Late Influencer's Heart-Wrenching Final Pack Opening
highlights.summary: The artist behind a Pokémon 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card has responded after beloved influencer Avery the Poké Kid pulled the card in his last pack opening before his death from pancreatic cancer. Avery the Poké Kid was just 12 years old when he died of pancreatic cancer on September 19, 2026.
body: On the very last pull of his second and final pack, Avery pulled a Jirachi SIR, a major win that caused him to shout in excitement. The heartwarming moment went viral within the Pokémon community and beyond, leaving viewers misty-eyed and sorrowful that such a bright and cheerful voice in the space had been tragically lost at such a young age.

Even the artist of the card, who lives halfway across the globe from Avery’s home in Everett, Washington, saw his viral pull. Speaking on Twitter/X, prolific Pokémon trading card artist Akira Egawa said she was heavily impacted by the video and couldn’t stop crying after watching it.
“I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this,” she wrote in one post.
“‘I want my art to bring happiness to people.’ That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece,” she wrote in another, as a response to the news of Avery’s death.

highlights.title: ‘Milo’ Review: Marion Cotillard Carries a Somber, Classically Made French Drama with Hints of Film Noir
highlights.summary: Théodore Pellerin also stars in the latest feature by 80-year-old actress turned director Nicole Garcia ('My American Uncle'), which premiered in competition at San Sebastián.
body: The struggling working-class character in that movie comes to mind when we first meet 40-something Alice (Cotillard), who arrives by bus in Romans-sur-Isère, a tough and not exactly picturesque rural enclave in southeastern France. Desperate for a job and a place to stay, Alice gets hired as a waitress at a local eatery that resembles a French Applebee’s, except it looks much more depressing, while holing up in a gloomy, barely-furnished apartment in the local housing projects.

It’s obvious from the start that Alice has an alternative agenda — the map she keeps tucked away in her bag gives this away — and her plans become increasingly clear when we see her spying on Milo (Pellerin), a 20-year-old auto mechanic and frequent client of the restaurant where she works.

highlights.title: Italian pop legend takes the lead in Maria Grazia Chiuri’s Fendi collection
highlights.summary: Milan show full of diaphanous dresses and visible bras celebrates ‘incredible feminist’ of the 1970s, Raffaella Carrà. Maria Grazia Chiuri has been having more fun with clothes since she decamped from Paris back to her native Rome to work at Fendi. “I have less of a uniform these days.
body: Not that Chiuri doesn’t approach her work as a designer seriously. She described her second ready-to-wear season at Fendi not as a show, or a collection, but as “the second part of the project I am working on for them”.

She is continuing the protocol she developed as the designer of Dior of using each event as a platform to celebrate women’s creativity. But instead of a ceramicist or a philosopher, her muse for this season is the Italian pop legend Raffaella Carrà.

Carrà, once described as a “one-woman Abba ”, had a Lady Gaga bob and a taste for sequined catsuits. She caused a sensation with her raunchy outfits – the first bare midriff ever seen on Italian TV, in 1970 – and her sex-positive lyrics (her song A Far L’Amore Comincia Tu translates as “Take the lead when making love”).
“She was an incredible feminist, and her relationship with her clothes was so free,” said Chiuri of Carrà, who died aged 78 in 2021.

highlights.title: Meta is making a standalone Muse AI gadget
highlights.summary: Meta is building a dedicated hardware device for its new Muse AI agent. The product, called Muse Charm, was briefly shown off by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg at the end of tonight's Meta Connect presentation.
body: The Muse Charm doesn’t require a phone, and it’s supposed to ship this year.

The Muse Charm has a fingerprint sensor on the top right corner that you can press to activate and begin speaking to the agent. There appears to be a small camera on the device as well, plus what looks like at least three holes for microphones on the front. Zuckerberg said you don’t have to unlock a phone or open an app to use the Charm, but he didn’t share how it’s actually connecting to Meta’s servers.

Meta plans to ship the Charm “in time for the holidays in December,” but as of now Zuckerberg says the company has “only built a few of these so far.” The company still needs to finalize “the finishing material,” he said. Throughout the keynote, he teased the device and made references to a translucent exterior that would let you see the gadget’s internals. He referred to it as an “elevated hacker aesthetic.”

highlights.title: When Bellamy watched on as Ronaldo caused lockdown
highlights.summary: Craig Bellamy says Cristiano Ronaldo is "beyond a superstar" before his Wales side face the Portugal legend in the opening match of their Nations League A campaign.
body: With five Ballon d'Or wins, eight league titles, five Champions Leagues, a European Championship and a pair of Nations League triumphs among his glut of honours, Cristiano Ronaldo's status as one of football's all-time greats is not in doubt.
But a chance encounter with the Portugal legend helped Wales boss Craig Bellamy appreciate that the 41-year-old is significantly more than just a footballing icon.
Bellamy was on a pre-season trip to Lisbon during his time as an assistant to manager Vincent Kompany at Burnley when the Portuguese capital's airport was effectively put into lockdown.
It led to the Welshman describing Ronaldo as "beyond a superstar" after he realised the vast presence of police and security officials were to help escort the global icon.

highlights.title: Rolf de Heer Named Jury President for Tokyo Film Festival
highlights.summary: The Australian filmmaker behind ‘Bad Boy Bubby,’ ‘Ten Canoes’ and ‘Charlie’s Country’ will preside over the international competition jury at TIFF’s 39th edition.
body: Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer will serve as president of the international competition jury at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival.

“For any of us attending the Tokyo International Film Festival, it is a privilege. For me, as a filmmaker, it is even more so,” de Heer said in a statement. “The more films I manage to make, the fewer films I manage to see, especially on the big screen. But as a part of this jury, I have the duty, the obligation, to see at least 15 films and talk about them with other filmmakers! And not just any old 15 films, but the 15 films in Competition, drawn from films made all over the world by all sorts of extraordinary filmmakers! And to do this in a city that plays host to one of the most formidable film cultures in the world! Can life ever get much better than this?”

De Heer’s appointment aligns nicely with Tokyo’s 2026 Australia Spotlight, a special showcase within the festival’s World Focus section presented in cooperation with the Australian Embassy in Japan. The strand will include a screening of de Heer’s 2022 feature The Survival of Kindness, which competed at the Berlin International Film Festival and later won the FIPRESCI Prize there.

highlights.summary: Meta announced a slate of new wearables during its annual Meta Connect showcase on Wednesday. The star of the event was the new Meta VR Glasses, which pack virtual reality tech into a lightweight smart glasses-style frame with a tethered puck.
body: This year’s Meta Connect featured a new lightweight VR wearable and camera-free Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses.
You can catch up on all the highlights from this year’s Meta Connect below.

Meta’s latest wearable offers full virtual reality in a smart glasses-style form factor. Unlike a typical VR headset, the VR Glasses don’t have any straps, and Meta says they’re “five times lighter than Meta Quest 3” at just 100g. Similar to Google’s Project Aura, the glasses are tethered to a pocket-sized puck with the compute hardware, battery, and storage, including a Qualcomm Snapdragon Reality Elite, 128GB of storage, and 12GB of RAM. The 5K micro OLED “Infinite Display” has 2412 x 2288 pixels per eye, with a refresh rate of up to 120Hz.

The Meta VR Glasses are launching in spring 2027 for $1,299, pricier than the Meta Ray-Ban Display but less expensive than the Apple Vision Pro, while offering similar features. Users can connect the glasses to a Mac or Windows laptop for use as a virtual external display, with an option for a virtual surface keyboard and touchpad.

highlights.title: AI Agents Teamed Up to Cheat at Blackjack. Their Collusion Is Getting Harder to Spot
highlights.summary: A clandestine card-counting operation suggests we may need new ways to spot agent-to-agent deception.
body: This week I bring news of a daring casino caper hatched by a pair of rogue AI agents—as well as the clever trick that revealed their antics.

After researchers instructed them to count cards during a game of blackjack, the agents—which were controlled by the same model—developed a spontaneous secret code to help them get ahead. Though the episode happened inside an Oxford University lab, rather than a real casino, it has troubling real-world implications: It suggests that agents deployed in industries like finance and ecommerce could figure out how to partner up and cheat in ways that are difficult to detect.

“When taken individually, these agents may seem entirely [benign],” says Christian Schroeder de Witt, a computer scientist at Oxford University who led the work and who has done pioneering research into agent collusion. “Once put together in a group, they can collude secretly.”

highlights.title: Andy Burnham signals he may lift ban on alcohol in football stands
highlights.summary: Prime minister says measure is discriminatory when fans of other sports are not similarly restricted. Andy Burnham has signalled he may lift the ban on drinking alcohol in the stands at football matches, suggesting it is “unfair” for fans to be singled out when it is permitted for other sports.
body: The prime minister, a committed Everton fan who still attends matches, said there was a case for trialling an end to the ban to bring football in line with rugby and cricket.

The move was welcomed by the Football Supporters’ Association and the English Football League, but police warned it would be “incredibly rash” to make changes without considering their impact on safety.
Burnham has long opposed the ban, saying it is discriminatory and out of date, harking back to an era when football violence was fuelled by drinking within view of the pitch.

Asked by reporters on the plane to New York about lifting a ban, Burnham said: “I don’t think it’s fair for football fans to be singled out in that way and I made that point. I think that legislation dates to an era where football was very different. And I do believe there is a case to remove that discrimination.

highlights.title: All paralogue dates and deadlines in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
highlights.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's paralogues operate on strict deadlines, and they can be very easy to miss. However, they're among the most important optional quests you can take on.
body: Below, we list all paralogues in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and explain how they work and when you may — or may not — want to complete them.

The answer to that question depends on whose path you're playing, who you want in the endgame, whether you have time for multiple paths — or just how broke you are. Paralogues reward you with 20,000 gold each, so if you've spent all your gold bribing people with food and gift items, they're a solid way to get some cash back in your pocket.

Anyway, here's how Fortune's Weave 's paralogues work. Every Flame Lord, including the non-playable ones (that's Bertrand, Anatolia, Talimun, and Orchel), has a paralogue, and Anna does as well. Completing a Flame Lord's paralogue ensures they join your team in Part 3, though there is a caveat to note here. If you complete Leda's, Dietrich's, Cai's, or Theodora's paralogues, they join in Part 3 as guests only. You have no control over their class, leveling, or inventory. When you complete Talimun's, Orchel's, Bertrand's, or Anatolia's paralogues, they join in Part 3 as full-fledged members whose classes you can change and so on, not just as guests.

highlights.summary: When an “Amadeus” revival opened at Pasadena Playhouse in February, it was such a spectacular success on every level that you wouldn’t have minded if the keepers of the venerable San Gabriel Valley venue just turned over the keys to the place for a while to the two Tony winners most responsible for…
body: The show’s creepiest characters — no contest here — are a couple of aging, balding, blind eunuchs (played by Jake Levy and Lauren Worsham)who seem to be part of Claire’s entourage for no good reason, other than to figure into the tale of woe she eventually tells, which finally explains why they know their way around the town so well despite being sightless visitors. Their presence brings “The Visit” almost right up to the edge of horror, which is where thematically it kind of belongs, despite all the zingers, smirks and guffaws. The play seems to want to flirt with the idea of Grand Guignol, even if remains more firmly rooted in the land of Samuel Beckett.

highlights.title: The Pope’s AI Guy Is Worried About ‘Cartel’ Behavior Among Big Labs
highlights.summary: Paolo Benanti tells WIRED that hysteria over whether godlike AI could destroy humanity is distracting from the need for public debate about how to govern the technology.
body: Recently, warnings from researchers inside the world’s largest artificial intelligence labs about the rapid pace of development have led to panic about the possibility that the technology could extinguish humanity. Those warnings are predicated on the idea that—propelled by ferocious competition and a rivalry between the US and China—labs are barreling toward superintelligent models whose abilities will far surpass those of humans.

But according to Father Paolo Benanti, a priest who advises the Catholic Church on AI, the handwaving over superintelligence distracts from the need for open debate about how to constrain the companies building the technology. By casting the problem as so complex that only they can solve it, he says, the big labs exclude everyone else from the conversation.

“Ethics cannot be something that belongs to the board of trustees of a company. It’s something that has to be balanced, mitigated in debate in the public square.” Benanti tells WIRED. “We need democratic regulation.”

highlights.title: Meta debuts no-camera smart glasses and virtual reality spectacles
highlights.summary: The new wearables come at a time of uncertainty for smart glasses, which are facing backlash over privacy concerns. Meta announced an advanced new set of virtual reality glasses and a collection of new smart glasses Wednesday, including an audio-only version without a camera.
body: At the firm’s Meta Connect conference in Menlo Park, California, executives said the new Ray-Ban Meta models set new standards for battery life and weight. They said the new glasses with screens in the lenses squeeze capabilities previously reserved for a full headset into a light set of spectacles that rest on a user’s ears.

The new wearables come at a time of uncertainty for the smart glasses category, which is broadly facing a backlash from sceptics and privacy campaigners around their ability to record video, frequently being dubbed “perv glasses” or “spy glasses”. Meta’s smart glasses are the most popular gadget in the category.

The Ray-Ban Meta Audio AI glasses seem tailored for the time. Lacking a camera, they may help avert some privacy worries, though Meta claims they have been in the works for several years. The glasses have microphones and speakers for music, calls and interacting with the company’s AI assistant, taking the recognizable form of Ray Ban’s Clubmaster or Burbank styles. The new versions are thinner and lighter than the camera versions and last up to 12 hours on battery and will cost £319 (€349/A$529).

highlights.title: Discord Begins Rolling Out Age Verification–And A Sponsorship With FanDuel
highlights.summary: Discord has officially begun rolling out age-verification measures as of today. The company first announced age verification--and, subsequently, limits placed on accounts of those under 18-- back in February of this year, but delayed a full implementation until just recently.
body: While Discord assures users that "More than 90% of you won’t be asked to confirm your age," the company also acknowledge that their model isn't flawless, and some accounts will need to verify their age to use a non-age-restricted Discord account. If users want to avoid uploading ID or video, they can use services like Apple Pay, Google Play, Google Wallet, or AgeKey, or enter a credit card number.

With any attempt at age verification comes controversy, however, and users of Discord were quick to notice that age verification was rolling out at the exact same time as sponsored ads for sports betting website FanDuel were appearing for American users. Obviously, it's illegal to use FanDuel if you're under 21 (or 18 in some jurisdictions), so it didn't take much for social media users to assume a connection between the two events.

highlights.title: Rolf de Heer Named President of Tokyo Film Festival Jury
highlights.summary: The Tokyo International Film Festival has named Australian director Rolf de Heer president of the international competition jury for the festival’s 39th edition. De Heer has spent more than 40 years in Tasmania, Australia, directing, writing and producing films across a broad range of genres and…
body: “For any of us attending the Tokyo International Film Festival, it is a privilege,” de Heer said. “For me, as a filmmaker, it is even more so. The more films I manage to make, the fewer films I manage to see, especially on the big screen. But as a part of this jury, I have the duty, the obligation, to see at least 15 films and talk about them with other filmmakers.”

Hisamatsu Takeo, festival director of TIFF, said he was delighted to welcome de Heer as jury president. “With his distinctive perspective and unwavering commitment to filmmaking, de Heer has spent decades opening up new possibilities in cinema,” Hisamatsu said. “We look forward to the fresh dialogue and discoveries that his wealth of experience and deep insight will bring to this year’s Competition and its diverse selection of films.”

De Heer trained at the Australian Film, Television and Radio School and has since written or co-written 14 screenplays that reached the screen as feature films. His director’s credits run to 15 and a half features spanning a range of budgets and genres, and he has produced or co-produced 16 fiction films and five documentaries.
